Monday. Damini's old laptop bag had split at the seam. In the hostel room, her roommate Simran had spent three evenings the week before comparing forty bags online for herself. Damini watched and thought, I have end-sems in twelve days. I can't give this three evenings.
She wrote two lines on a sticky note: under 1,200 rupees, padded laptop pocket. Nothing else.
Wednesday. At the market near the college gate, the second shop had a grey bag for 950 with a thick padded sleeve. She checked both lines on the note and paid. The whole trip took twenty-five minutes.
Saturday. Simran was still scrolling reviews. Damini was on her third chapter of circuit theory, the grey bag hanging on the chair. "It holds the laptop," she said. "That's all I needed from it."

qa.q: How much did the grey bag cost?
qa.a: The grey bag at the second shop was 950.

qa.q: What was Damini thinking as she watched Simran compare forty bags?
qa.a: She felt anxious about her end-sems in twelve days and decided she couldn't spend three evenings on a bag.

qa.q: When would Damini's two-line approach not be enough?
qa.a: For something big or long-lasting, like a laptop itself, she might need more criteria and more time to compare.

qa.q: How might Simran see Damini's quick purchase?
qa.a: Simran may be surprised or even a little envious, since she is still scrolling reviews while Damini is already studying.

grounding: It shows a hostel student choosing a bag by two criteria and stopping, saving hours for exam preparation.

Amandeep, you're lost in phone comparisons again. Let your Deepak Mamu tell you something from hostel days.
Second year engineering, my trunk lock broke two weeks before exams, and I needed a laptop bag to keep my borrowed laptop safe. My friend Harjot spent a whole weekend at every shop in Sector 17 for his bag. Came back with the perfect one and a backlog in maths.
I asked myself one thing. What does this bag actually need to do? Keep the laptop from cracking, and cost less than what I had in my pocket. Two conditions. That's all.
The first shop I entered had a black one with a padded pocket, within my money. I bought it and went back to studying. Used it for six years.
For small things, beta, good enough is good. Save your brain for exams.

qa.q: How long did Deepak use the bag?
qa.a: He used it for six years.

qa.q: How might Deepak have felt walking out of the first shop with the bag?
qa.a: He probably felt relieved and satisfied, free to go back to studying instead of spending the weekend searching.

qa.q: At the moment Harjot set out to visit every shop, what else could he have done?
qa.a: Harjot could have set two simple checks for the bag and bought the first match, keeping the weekend for maths.

qa.q: How did Harjot's choice affect him?
qa.a: Harjot got the perfect bag but a backlog in maths, which shows what the long search cost.
